narration.text: A black hole is a dark sphere hanging in empty space.
Its edge is a one-way boundary, not a solid wall.
Hot gas circling outside it glows brightly.
Its gravity bends that light into a bright ring around a dark shadow.
Gravity pulls hardest on the nearest side of anything falling in.
A falling object is drawn out long and thin.

style.text: bright, well-exposed space imagery like a planetarium film: the subject is large, lit and moving from the first frame, warm glowing colours, slow continuous camera drift, no fade in from black

brief.title: A boundary, not a surface
brief.summary: A black hole's edge is a one-way boundary, not a solid surface: what we see from far away, and what a falling object would feel.
